pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

Local CyDoc documentation#

Both desktop interfaces open the same packaged CyDoc reader in the system browser using a file:// URL. Help > User guide opens the home page; F1 and contextual help open the active workspace's chapter. Help works without a project and during project operations. No HTTP server, CDN, browser engine or Node.js runtime is shipped for reading.

Content and languages#

documentation/manual/en and fr contain 48 matching guides. Frontmatter page IDs and explicit heading IDs are shared between translations. English is the default. The host chooses the application language, then English, then the original language for references that have no English version. CyDoc owns search, history, themes, language switching and reading positions. Browser storage restrictions can prevent position persistence; navigation still works.

documentation/references.json imports 38 existing technical documents and historical release notes without replacing their original sources. Historical pages are labelled. References retain their maintained language: 26 need French translations and 12 need English translations. The generated References and coverage page records these gaps and repository-only exclusions. CyDoc's standard translation report tracks the English originals (26 missing, zero outdated); three bilingual annotation pages are untracked because the pinned extractor does not carry revision metadata.

Guides use revision (English) and sourceRevision (French) to track synchronization. Preserve page, heading and image IDs when translating. documentation/routes.json maps workspaces and the former Help tab to page IDs. Legacy doc:page-id#section references and configured aliases remain supported. Reader routes are #/locale/page-id/section?media=image-id.

Modules, media and source API#

Only image is enabled: screenshots, localized SVG diagrams, zoom, annotations and in-reader enlargement. Static diagrams do not require graph. Existing content has no videos, animated guides, 3D models or interactive node graphs, so video, gif, mesh, gallery and graph are omitted. Three.js is not an application dependency. Escape exits enlarged media without creating a window; CyDoc supplies keyboard focus, touch interactions and zoom controls.

Assets live in documentation/assets. scripts/render-documentation-media.py generates 13 English/French SVG diagrams and PNG companions from scripts/documentation-diagrams.json, and copies demonstration screenshots from docs/images. Pillow is an authoring dependency only. Add local media using CyDoc fenced image blocks with stable IDs and translated captions.

documentation/source-scope.json limits the distributed source index to two public C# plugin-contract files and the native documentation-link contract. Bilingual @doc annotations generate API pages. The index is lexical: no interpretation of C# XML comments, overload resolution or C++ macro expansion. Server API and plugin examples are also retained as references. Application data, validation, services and Undo/Redo remain outside CyDoc.

Generate and check#

Generation requires Node.js 22+ and npm. The official CyDoc npm archive is vendored and pinned by revision and SHA-256 in documentation/cydoc.lock.json. Builds do not require private GitHub access. npm installs locked authoring/test dependencies when needed; installed applications need neither npm nor Internet access.

From the repository root:

sh
node documentation/build.mjsnode documentation/build.mjs --checknode --test documentation/test/*.test.mjsdotnet test CyRevision.sln -c Release

python scripts/build-documentation.py [--check] remains a compatibility wrapper. --ensure validates inputs and output hashes and rebuilds only when needed. Desktop builds run it before copying resources. The official exporter resolves resources and bundles the image provider; the host adds a CSP, palette, favicon, license and coverage metadata without modifying library bundles or compiled page data.

The generated, versioned reader is src/CyRevision.Desktop/Help. Desktop build/publish outputs copy it recursively, including portable packages and installers. Keep the whole Help directory: data.js, viewer.js, media-image.js, styles and assets. Regenerate after changing inputs. Generated staging folders documentation/content-build, documentation/source-api and artifacts/cydoc-export are not sources.

Integration verification#

Managed tests cover every workspace route, locale fallback, legacy aliases, sections/media IDs, installation paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters, unavailable readers and help during busy operations. Native tests cover F1, callbacks, locales, the launch surface and non-reader URL rejection without opening a browser. Node tests validate compiled links/resources, translation parity, source scope and modules. A DOM fixture exercises actual CyDoc navigation and image controls with script/resource loading and navigation disabled; it is not a browser rendering test.

For a local published build, check real IPC without opening a browser:

sh
python scripts/test_offline_guide.py --engine artifacts/native-v2-cydoc/CyRevision.Desktop.exedotnet run --project tests/CyRevision.Guide.UiChecks -c Release -- artifacts/cydoc-verification

The second command checks/captures the Classic launch surface only. Before shipping on each target, manually open Help/index.html and test F1/context links, both languages, search, anchors, image focus/enlargement/Escape, touch/zoom, themes, narrow layouts, DPI and reading-position restoration. Verify offline with networking disabled. Real file:// transport, image decoding and browser storage require a target browser; DOM fixtures cannot establish those properties.

Windows host builds and automated tests are available. Linux/macOS retain the Classic publish path but need target-platform browser/rendering checks. Native V2 remains Windows/Direct3D 11. CyDoc source/license: MrMybal/CyDoc (MIT; repository access may be required).

pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

Perforce Helix Core integration#

CyRevision ships an optional, project-scoped Perforce plugin. It uses the official p4 command-line client and does not embed a Perforce server or an alternative protocol implementation.

Safety model#

  • The plugin is disabled by default and must be enabled separately for each CyRevision project.
  • Enabling it does not initialize, convert, reconcile, sync, or otherwise modify the project.
  • CyRevision stores only the executable path and the P4PORT, P4USER, and P4CLIENT coordinates in its application configuration.
  • Passwords, tickets, and trust material remain managed by the official Perforce tools and are never written to the project or the CyRevision plugin settings.
  • Workspace-writing actions are disabled by default. The user must validate the server, login ticket, and workspace mapping, then explicitly enable writes.
  • Reconcile and sync offer non-writing previews. Reconcile, sync, revert, and submit require confirmation in the desktop interface.
  • Every file operation is restricted to the selected CyRevision project root.

Available tools#

  • detect the official p4 CLI;
  • validate server access, authentication, and the selected client workspace;
  • list files opened by the current or other workspaces;
  • search opened files by path, action, user, workspace, or changelist;
  • list pending and recently submitted changelists;
  • inspect a selected file's revision history;
  • preview and apply p4 reconcile;
  • open a selected project file for edit;
  • revert unchanged files or explicitly revert a selected file;
  • preview and apply workspace sync;
  • submit the default or a selected numbered changelist.

First configuration#

  1. Install the Helix Core Command-Line Client and authenticate from a trusted terminal with p4 login.
  2. Enable Perforce Helix Core from Extensions & Help > Plugins for the selected project.
  3. Enter or verify P4PORT, P4USER, and P4CLIENT in the Perforce tab.
  4. Select Validate & refresh. CyRevision verifies that the client root contains the selected project.
  5. Only if the result is correct, enable Enable workspace writes and save the project configuration.

The plugin also contributes a dedicated Perforce operating mode. This mode disables Git features, keeps backups available, and exposes the Perforce, solution explorer, console, and backup tools.

pages.title: CyRevision plugin and app API
pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

CyRevision plugin and app API#

CyRevision extensions are packaged separately and enabled for each project. Enabling a package for one project does not expose its tabs, file providers, project modes, or services in another project.

Extension contracts#

Reference CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions and implement ICyRevisionPlugin. Optional interfaces add narrowly-scoped capabilities:

  • IFilePresentationProvider adds previews and diffs everywhere CyRevision displays a file;
  • IProjectModeProvider contributes a complete operating mode and its workspace tabs;
  • IProjectScopedPlugin receives activation and deactivation for one project;
  • IWorkItemIntegrationPlugin searches a project-scoped issue tracker and returns stable references for commit and pull-request drafts without exposing credentials to Git;
  • engine, AI, Lore, and Perforce interfaces expose their dedicated integration surfaces.

The package contains cyrevision-plugin.json, an entry assembly, and an entry type. UI-independent records keep plugins decoupled from Avalonia.

The bundled Jira, ClickUp, and CyTask connectors are reference implementations of IWorkItemIntegrationPlugin. They store only project-scoped server/scope settings; tokens remain in memory or are read from a named environment variable.

Project file sandbox#

Project-scoped extensions should access files through IPluginProjectFileSandbox. The host policy grants only explicit operations and relative roots. The broker rejects absolute paths, .. traversal, disallowed roots, oversized reads/writes, and symbolic links escaping the project. Writes use a temporary file followed by an atomic replacement.

An in-process .NET DLL is trusted code and is not an operating-system security boundary: it could call System.IO, networking, or process APIs directly. Plugins needing hard isolation must run as an external app/worker process. The future app host will map declared network and process capabilities to an isolated process; CyRevision never presents the in-process broker as a complete OS sandbox.

Safety rules#

  • default to read-only permissions;
  • ask separately for write, network, and process capabilities;
  • store project configuration under CyRevision data directories, not in Git;
  • never persist passwords, API keys, session tokens, or WireGuard private keys in a plugin manifest;
  • disable every project surface immediately when its plugin is disabled;
  • return a preview before performing a destructive or remote operation.

pages.title: CyRevision plugins and Unreal integration
pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

CyRevision plugins and Unreal integration#

CyRevision plugins are separate .NET assemblies discovered from the Plugins directory beside the application. Their manifests use cyrevision-plugin.json, and enabled plugin identifiers are stored in the current user's CyRevision configuration. A packaged plugin may therefore remain present without being loaded.

The release contains two distinct Unreal components:

Component Runs in Required
CyRevision.Plugin.Unreal CyRevision No; disabled by default
CyRevisionUnreal Unreal Editor No; autonomous after installation

Installing the Unreal Editor plugin#

  1. Open Plugins in CyRevision.
  2. Select Unreal Engine Integration and choose Enable.
  3. Select a .uproject file.
  4. Choose Install / update in project.

CyRevision detects the project's Unreal version and whether it is a C++ or Blueprint-only project before enabling installation. It displays the complete compatibility list and blocks a mismatched or unavailable package.

Project type Installation mode Compatibility
C++ Portable source plugin, compiled by the project's Editor target Unreal 4.27 and 5.0 through 5.8
Blueprint-only Exact precompiled plugin for the engine minor version and OS Win64 variants currently bundled for Unreal 5.2 through 5.8

CyRevision copies the selected plugin into Project/Plugins/CyRevisionUnreal, adds an enabled plugin entry to the .uproject descriptor, and keeps a .cyrevision.bak copy of that descriptor. When updating an existing plugin, its previous directory is moved to Saved/CyRevision/PluginBackups before the new copy is activated.

C++ projects must regenerate project files and compile the Editor target. Blueprint-only projects do not compile the plugin, so CyRevision requires the exact precompiled variant and refuses installation when it is absent. Unreal 4.27, 5.0, and 5.1 are source-compatible targets, but their Blueprint-only Win64 variants are not yet bundled.

Autonomous Unreal mode#

The Unreal plugin does not require the desktop client. Tools > Revision dashboard can show repository status and recent revisions, stage all files, commit, fetch, pull, and push by using the configured Git executable. Advisory reservations also remain available locally or through the project's existing shared presence directory.

Direct connection#

Tools > Swarm over VPN is autonomous too. On Windows it can save the Coordinator VPN IPv4/DNS alias to the existing Swarm Agent options, create a .cyrevision.bak copy first, launch Agent or Coordinator, test TCP 8008/8009, and show a manual recovery guide. The optional desktop plugin adds WireGuard peer discovery, project-scoped firewall/DNS changes and a combined configuration diagnostic.

The CyRevision Unreal extension listens on 127.0.0.1:47832 only while it is enabled and CyRevision is open. Configuring a project creates a random token and writes it to Saved/CyRevision/bridge.json. This file is outside normal source-controlled project content and should remain excluded from Git.

Unreal sends the token as a Bearer credential. A successful connection lets it announce Git and advisory changes so CyRevision can refresh the matching project. The bridge advertises Swarm and VPN-file capabilities but does not grant them: no Git, LFS, Sync, backup, VPN, DNS, firewall or file-transfer permission is granted by the bridge token itself.

Disabling the CyRevision plugin stops and unloads the bridge. It does not remove CyRevisionUnreal from any project, and the Unreal-side autonomous tools continue to work.

Local Unreal build lab#

When the optional Unreal integration is enabled, Extensions & Help > Unreal builds discovers:

  • Unreal installations registered with Epic Launcher or Unreal Engine\Builds;
  • additional roots listed in CYREVISION_UNREAL_ENGINE_ROOTS;
  • project targets declared by *.Target.cs;
  • every project plugin containing a .uplugin descriptor.

The build lab can compile one engine or a selected engine-version range. It runs Unreal Build Tool for compile checks, Automation Tool BuildPlugin for plugins, and BuildCookRun when Cook & package is selected. Standard output and error are streamed into the project task and log views. Exit code 0 is success; every other code is reported as a failed row with its retained log path.

Discovery is cached below Project/.cyrevision/cache/unreal and invalidated when the .uproject, targets, plugins or toolchain environment changes. Discover forces a new scan when an installation was added manually. Named build presets retain the target, platform, configuration and toolchain choices per project.

The live log is a bounded, virtualized list rather than one continuously rebuilt text block. Compiler and Automation Tool output is also parsed into structured diagnostics with severity, file, line and error code. Version matrices remain sequential by default; an explicit parallel limit from 2 to 4 is available for machines with enough CPU, RAM and disk bandwidth.

Windows, Linux cross-compilation, and Android targets are available. CyRevision reads each engine's Build.version, recommends the matching Epic Linux toolchain/Clang generation, inspects LINUX_MULTIARCH_ROOT, LINUX_ROOT, AutoSDK, Android SDK/NDK and JAVA_HOME, and lets the user override those paths per project. pages.text: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows. CyRevision plugins and Unreal integration # CyRevision plugins are separate .NET assemblies discovered from the Plugins directory beside the application. Their manifests use cyrevision-plugin.json , and enabled plugin identifiers are stored in the current user's CyRevision configuration. A packaged plugin may therefore remain present without being loaded. The release contains two distinct Unreal components: Component Runs in Required CyRevision.Plugin.Unreal CyRevision No; disabled by default CyRevisionUnreal Unreal Editor No; autonomous after installation Installing the Unreal Editor plugin # Open Plugins in CyRevision. Select Unreal Engine Integration and choose Enable . Select a .uproject file. Choose Install / update in project . CyRevision detects the project's Unreal version and whether it is a C++ or Blueprint-only project before enabling installation. It displays the complete compatibility list and blocks a mismatched or unavailable package. Project type Installation mode Compatibility C++ Portable source plugin, compiled by the project's Editor target Unreal 4.27 and 5.0 through 5.8 Blueprint-only Exact precompiled plugin for the engine minor version and OS Win64 variants currently bundled for Unreal 5.2 through 5.8 CyRevision copies the selected plugin into Project/Plugins/CyRevisionUnreal , adds an enabled plugin entry to the .uproject descriptor, and keeps a .cyrevision.bak copy of that descriptor. When updating an existing plugin, its previous directory is moved to Saved/CyRevision/PluginBackups before the new copy is activated. C++ projects must regenerate project files and compile the Editor target. Blueprint-only projects do not compile the plugin, so CyRevision requires the exact precompiled variant and refuses installation when it is absent. Unreal 4.27, 5.0, and 5.1 are source-compatible targets, but their Blueprint-only Win64 variants are not yet bundled. Autonomous Unreal mode # The Unreal plugin does not require the desktop client. Tools > Revision dashboard can show repository status and recent revisions, stage all files, commit, fetch, pull, and push by using the configured Git executable. Advisory reservations also remain available locally or through the project's existing shared presence directory. Direct connection # Tools > Swarm over VPN is autonomous too. On Windows it can save the Coordinator VPN IPv4/DNS alias to the existing Swarm Agent options, create a .cyrevision.bak copy first, launch Agent or Coordinator, test TCP 8008/8009, and show a manual recovery guide. The optional desktop plugin adds WireGuard peer discovery, project-scoped firewall/DNS changes and a combined configuration diagnostic. The CyRevision Unreal extension listens on 127.0.0.1:47832 only while it is enabled and CyRevision is open. Configuring a project creates a random token and writes it to Saved/CyRevision/bridge.json . This file is outside normal source-controlled project content and should remain excluded from Git. Unreal sends the token as a Bearer credential. A successful connection lets it announce Git and advisory changes so CyRevision can refresh the matching project. The bridge advertises Swarm and VPN-file capabilities but does not grant them: no Git, LFS, Sync, backup, VPN, DNS, firewall or file-transfer permission is granted by the bridge token itself. Disabling the CyRevision plugin stops and unloads the bridge. It does not remove CyRevisionUnreal from any project, and the Unreal-side autonomous tools continue to work. Local Unreal build lab # When the optional Unreal integration is enabled, Extensions & Help > Unreal builds discovers: Unreal installations registered with Epic Launcher or Unreal Engine\Builds ; additional roots listed in CYREVISION_UNREAL_ENGINE_ROOTS ; project targets declared by *.Target.cs ; every project plugin containing a .uplugin descriptor. The build lab can compile one engine or a selected engine-version range. It runs Unreal Build Tool for compile checks, Automation Tool BuildPlugin for plugins, and BuildCookRun when Cook & package is selected. Standard output and error are streamed into the project task and log views. Exit code 0 is success; every other code is reported as a failed row with its retained log path. Discovery is cached below Project/.cyrevision/cache/unreal and invalidated when the .uproject , targets, plugins or toolchain environment changes. Discover forces a new scan when an installation was added manually. Named build presets retain the target, platform, configuration and toolchain choices per project. The live log is a bounded, virtualized list rather than one continuously rebuilt text block. Compiler and Automation Tool output is also parsed into structured diagnostics with severity, file, line and error code. Version matrices remain sequential by default; an explicit parallel limit from 2 to 4 is available for machines with enough CPU, RAM and disk bandwidth. pages.title: Pull request manager
pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

Pull request manager#

CyRevision includes an integrated pull request workspace. The first provider is GitHub and the service boundary is provider-neutral so GitLab, Forgejo, or a decentralized review provider can be added without redesigning the desktop interface.

Repository connection#

The manager reads the origin remote of the selected Git project. It supports GitHub HTTPS and SSH remotes, including GitHub Enterprise hosts. For enterprise installations, the API address can be overridden in the pull request toolbar.

Public pull requests can normally be read without authentication. Private repositories and write operations require a GitHub token. CyRevision resolves it from either:

  • a masked session-only field; or
  • the named environment variable, GITHUB_TOKEN by default.

The token is never written to the project, Git repository, or CyRevision settings. Prefer a fine-grained token limited to the repository with pull-request write permission and only the additional permissions your organization requires.

Workspace#

The Pull Requests tab provides:

  • open, closed, draft, or merged request lists with distinct colors, ownership markers, and the latest CI state;
  • title, author, branches, draft state, review state, and mergeability;
  • changed-file statistics and unified patches;
  • general comments and submitted reviews;
  • pull request creation from a head branch to a base branch;
  • comment, approve, request-changes, close, reopen, and merge actions;
  • merge, squash, and rebase strategies when allowed by the repository;
  • a direct link to the provider page;
  • a dedicated CI view with matching workflow runs, jobs, complete searchable logs, all/error/warning filters, a synchronized detached log window, workflow dispatch, failed-job reruns, and cancellation when permitted;
  • a non-destructive merge-conflict view that lists conflicting paths without checking out or merging either branch;
  • automatic Jira/ClickUp/CyTask link detection in the title, description, commits, comments, and reviews;
  • optional confirmed or automatic completion transitions for detected tasks after a successful merge;
  • confirmed removal of the merged local head branch after a Git safety analysis.

Line-level review comments are not part of the initial alpha implementation; reviews currently apply to the complete pull request.

CI, conflicts, and linked tasks#

The CI page associates workflow runs by pull-request head branch and commit SHA. Job data remains available even when the forge cannot provide the downloadable log archive. Logs are capped for interactive use, can be filtered to classified error or warning lines, searched by source, text, or line number, and opened in a non-modal synchronized window. Dispatch, rerun, and cancellation actions require the same session-only write token and always target the pull-request branch or selected run.

Conflict inspection fetches disposable private references under refs/cyrevision/inspect, analyzes them with git merge-tree, and removes those references after inspection. It does not switch branches, touch the index, or write a merge result into the working tree.

When a Jira, ClickUp, or CyTask plugin is enabled for the selected project, CyRevision recognizes provider URLs and task IDs across the complete pull-request discussion. After a successful merge, the per-project policy can ask before applying provider completion transitions, apply them automatically, or leave all tasks unchanged. Provider permissions and workflow-specific transition availability are revalidated for every task.

Safe checkout and remote changes#

Checkout refuses to run while the working tree contains changes. It fetches the pull request head into a dedicated remote-tracking reference and creates or fast-forwards a local cyrevision/pr-N branch. It never force-resets the current branch.

Merge, close, reopen, workflow dispatch, CI rerun, and task transitions affect remote services. CyRevision displays a confirmation before these actions because merging can trigger CI, deployment, or other repository automation. Provider errors are sanitized before display so credentials are not exposed.

After a merge, local branch removal is separate and optional. CyRevision first checks whether the branch is current, present in another worktree, merged into the current history, or fully published. The confirmation explains what retains its commits. It never deletes the remote branch.

Decentralized projects#

Git, Git LFS, Sync, backup, and peer exchange remain usable without GitHub. Pull requests are forge-backed review objects, so the current manager is available when a supported forge remote is detected. A future decentralized review adapter can use the same interface without making GitHub mandatory for the rest of CyRevision.

CyRevision 0.1.28 Alpha#

  • Introduced the Windows V2 interface built with Dear ImGui/CyUI, with a project-only sidebar, project-scoped workspaces, status indicators and orange active tabs.
  • Added detachable workspaces, lists, file previews and diffs in independent windows, with dock/return actions and saved layouts. Detached views follow the active project and share its engine.
  • Fixed project switching during background scans, history and comparison selection, stale file results and overlapping refresh requests.
  • Added visible loading indicators, queued-action feedback and cancellation while retaining guards against duplicate operations.
  • Ported Git/LFS, pull requests, CI logs, branch inspection, code search, asset previews, project services, plugins and preferences to the V2 workspace shell.
  • Improved Git process cancellation and export handling, workspace invalidation and searches over changing directories.

Windows installer shortcuts open the V2 interface; CyRevision (Classic) remains available for the previous Avalonia interface. In the portable ZIP, run CyRevision.Native.exe for V2 or CyRevision.Desktop.exe for Classic.

Linux and macOS continue to use the Avalonia interface. V2 requires Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 11; native tray/start-hidden integration is not yet available.

The V2 interface remains Alpha. Git features are Beta; Sync, Git + Sync, Lore, Backup and plugin features remain Alpha.

CyRevision 0.1.31 Alpha#

  • Restored the Windows V2 system tray: closing the main window hides the main and detached views while the engine and background services continue running.
  • Added tray commands to reopen CyRevision or quit completely through the existing confirmation dialog.
  • Kept engine requests responsive while the interface is hidden and paused rendering until the windows are restored.

  • Prevented isolated test profiles from changing system startup registration and avoided duplicate tray icons when saving preferences.

Windows V2 requires Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 11. In the portable ZIP, launch CyRevision.Native.exe; CyRevision.Desktop.exe and the CyRevision (Classic) installer shortcut remain available for the Avalonia interface. Linux and macOS continue to use Avalonia.

Windows V2 requires Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 11. Launch CyRevision.Native.exe from the portable ZIP. The CyRevision (Classic) shortcut and CyRevision.Desktop.exe remain available; Linux and macOS use the Avalonia interface. The V2 interface remains Alpha. Git features are Beta; Sync, Git + Sync, Lore, Backup and plugin features remain Alpha.

pages.title: Remote build agent
pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

Remote build agent#

CyRevision.Build.Agent runs beside the desktop application or on a Windows, Linux, or macOS CI/build machine. It does not require GitHub and never pushes a temporary branch.

First start#

Windows example from an installed release:

powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\CyRevision\BuildAgent\CyRevision.Build.Agent.exe' --print-token

Linux package example:

bash
cyrevision-build-agent --print-token

The first start creates a random 256-bit bearer token and a safe empty agent.json. Keep the token secret. The agent refuses all builds until a project and at least one recipe are configured locally.

Example agent.json#

json
{  "jobsRoot": "D:/CyRevisionBuildJobs",  "maximumParallelJobs": 1,  "completedJobRetentionHours": 72,  "projects": [    {      "projectId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",      "projectName": "My Unreal Project",      "workspaceRoot": "D:/BuildWorkspaces/MyProject",      "allowUploadedSnapshots": true,      "maximumSnapshotBytes": 107374182400,      "recipes": [        {          "id": "unreal-win64-development",          "displayName": "Unreal Win64 Development",          "executable": "C:/Windows/System32/cmd.exe",          "arguments": ["/d", "/s", "/c", "\"C:/Epic/UE_5.5/Engine/Build/BatchFiles/Build.bat\" MyProjectEditor Win64 Development -Project=MyProject.uproject -WaitMutex"],          "workingDirectory": ".",          "artifactPatterns": ["Binaries/Win64/**", "Saved/Logs/**"],          "timeoutMinutes": 180        }      ]    }  ]}

Copy the exact project ID shown in CyRevision's Remote builds tab. The executable, arguments, timeout, workspace and artifact patterns are controlled only by the build-machine operator. A client can select a recipe ID but cannot submit a command.

Network setup#

For local testing the agent listens on 127.0.0.1:47841. For another VPN peer, bind to the build machine's WireGuard IPv4 and add --allow-private-http, then enable Remote build agent over VPN in the firewall assistant. Do not create a modem/router forward for TCP 47841. Use HTTPS as well when transport leaves the trusted WireGuard tunnel.

Source modes#

  • ExistingWorkspace: no source upload. The agent uses workspaceRoot and rejects a different Git HEAD when both sides expose a Git repository. Use CyRevision Sync or another deliberate deployment step first.
  • UploadedSnapshot: tracked plus non-ignored working files are zipped. .git, Binaries, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, bin, obj, .idea, .vs, and node_modules are excluded. The agent extracts into a unique job directory with traversal and size checks.

After success, only files matched by artifactPatterns, plus build.log, are placed in the downloadable artifact ZIP. Jobs can be cancelled from CyRevision and each recipe has a hard timeout.

pages.title: Team chat over VPN or Sync
pages.description: Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.
pages.html:
Technical reference retained in its maintained language. Use the current guides for user workflows.

Team chat over VPN or Sync#

CyRevision includes a project-scoped team conversation under Team & Network > Team chat. It never changes the Git repository.

VPN transport#

One peer starts the host on its WireGuard IPv4 and TCP port 47843. Other peers enter that VPN address as their endpoint and copy the same 256-bit project token through a separate trusted channel. CyRevision refuses public listener and peer addresses, verifies the token in constant time, limits attachment size, and validates every attachment with SHA-256.

Conversation saving is optional for the VPN host. When enabled, messages and attachments are stored beneath the local CyRevision data directory for that project. When disabled, message history is kept only for the running host session; received attachments still use the local CyRevision receive cache so they can be opened safely.

VPN messages that cannot reach the host immediately are placed in a project-scoped local outbox. CyRevision reports their pending/failed state and retries them when the conversation is refreshed. The message list only transfers attachment metadata; the bytes are downloaded and SHA-256 verified when Open attachment is used.

Sync-folder transport#

Choose an existing synchronized folder. CyRevision creates a .cyrevision-chat subfolder and writes one immutable JSON file per message plus a separate content-addressed attachment location. It never appends several peers to one shared file, avoiding the conflict pattern of a synchronized JSONL/chat log. The folder may be a project-independent shared folder managed by CyRevision Sync.

Images and ordinary files use the same attachment mechanism. Select a received attachment and choose Open attachment to hand it to the operating system. Retention controls which archived messages are loaded; CyRevision does not silently delete older synchronized messages.

CyRevision keeps a disposable incremental index in Project/.cyrevision/cache/chat. Reopening a large conversation compares file metadata and parses only new or changed message files. A watcher refreshes an open Sync conversation after a short debounce, while presence files expose recently connected teammates without rescanning attachments.

Optional encryption at rest#

Enable Encrypt stored conversations to protect synchronized or locally archived message bodies and attachments with AES-256-GCM. The project chat token derives the encryption key and authenticated metadata prevents a ciphertext from being moved to another project unnoticed. Peers must therefore share the exact token through an already trusted channel. Losing that token makes the encrypted archive intentionally unrecoverable.

The cache and temporary decrypted attachment copies are local, disposable CyRevision data. They are never a replacement for the synchronized source of truth.

pages.title: Remote builds over VPN
pages.description: Run allowlisted builds on a CI machine and download artifacts without pushing a temporary branch.
pages.html:
Agent setup#

Install the packaged BuildAgent on the CI/build machine and run CyRevision.Build.Agent --print-token. The first run creates a token and a safe empty agent.json. Add the exact CyRevision project ID and one or more recipes. The agent operator owns the executable, arguments, timeout, workspace, and artifact patterns; a client can select only a recipe ID and can never submit a command.

Network#

Local testing uses 127.0.0.1:47841. For another peer, bind to the build machine's WireGuard IPv4, add --allow-private-http, and enable Remote build agent over VPN in the firewall assistant. Never forward TCP 47841 on the router.

Source modes#

ExistingWorkspace transfers no source and uses the configured workspace. If both sides have Git metadata, a different HEAD is rejected. UploadedSnapshot sends tracked and non-ignored working files but excludes .git and generated caches, then extracts into a unique path with traversal and size checks.

Run and download#

In Remote builds, enter the VPN endpoint, token, recipe ID, mode, and artifact destination. Test agent lists the allowlisted recipes. Start remote build follows the job log, supports cancellation, and downloads an artifact ZIP after success. Only recipe-declared files and build.log are returned; no commit or branch is pushed to a remote.

See also

pages.title: Multi Restore and cherry-pick composition
pages.description: Compose file versions or ordered commits with a safety preview before changing the working tree or a local branch.
pages.html:
Multi restore#

Open Compose > Multi restore, choose a commit, and load its changed files. Check only the files to include. BeforeCommit selects the state immediately before that commit; AtCommit selects the version stored by the commit. Adds, deletes, and renames become explicit restore or delete operations.

Safety preview#

Build safety preview before applying. The preview expires after fifteen minutes, verifies that HEAD has not moved, detects local changes, and blocks missing Git LFS objects. Application writes a timestamped recovery copy under the Git common directory before changing any path. The index is not modified and no commit or push is created.

Branch comparison#

Open Branch compare & cherry-pick, choose a source and an existing local target. Source-only, target-only, and patch-equivalent commits are shown separately, so an already applied change can be recognized even when its hash differs. Selected source-only commits are applied in the displayed order.

Cherry-pick modes#

KeepCommits preserves individual commits. CombineIntoOne applies their content and creates one commit with the supplied message. Merge commits are blocked until an explicit mainline workflow is available.

Isolation and conflicts#

If the target is not the active branch, CyRevision uses a temporary worktree and leaves the displayed branch untouched. A conflict aborts the operation and restores the target tip. Nothing is pushed automatically.

Detached windows#

View > Open detached workspace opens additional History, Code, Multi Restore, or Cherry-pick windows. Open several at once for multiple monitors; their project data and selection stay linked to the main window.

See also

pages.title: Safe LFS storage and cleanup
pages.description: Move the LFS cache to another disk and reclaim old objects without deleting the project's last copy.
pages.html:
Classification#

Open Git LFS > Storage & safe cleanup and run Analyze. Protected objects are reachable from local refs, stashes, indexes, or worktrees and are never selected. This includes commits and branches that have not been pushed. Eligible objects are orphaned, outside the grace period, and have the configured number of verified copies. Everything else is blocked.

Retention evidence#

A remote copy is accepted only after a Git LFS dry run with remote and unreachable-object verification. A peer copy requires a fresh signed inventory and an object actually published in the exchange store. An archive copy uses CyRevision's manifest and is SHA-256 checked again before deletion. With no remote, retain at least one peer or archive copy; require two or more for stronger redundancy.

Deleted prs and branches#

A branch deleted on a forge may still exist locally. Its objects stay protected until you deliberately remove the local ref. Once orphaned, Analyze decides whether another verified copy makes them eligible. A local-only PR or unpushed branch is always kept.

External storage#

Choose a dedicated empty directory, then relocate. CyRevision copies and hashes every object before setting the repository-local lfs.storage value. A repository ownership marker prevents unsafe shared stores. Keep the old cache for the first test, then enable removal only after checkout and Time Machine access succeed.

Cleanup#

Archive candidates creates verified copies without deleting. Analyze again, review each decision, then confirm cleanup. Plans expire after fifteen minutes, local references are rechecked, and an audit is written under .git/cyrevision/lfs-cleanup.

See also

pages.title: Shared folders outside the project
pages.description: Share only explicit folders with authorized peers.
pages.html:
Create a share#

Open Team & Network > Shared Sync folders. Choose a specific existing folder, a clear display name and the intended folder policy. Do not share a broad user profile, whole disk or unrelated project just to exchange a few files.

Admit participants#

  1. Check the selected project and authorized peer identity.
  2. Configure the folder's intended participants and policy.
  3. Start the dedicated synchronization service explicitly.
  4. Verify folder/device state and pending changes on each side.

A VPN connection does not grant synchronized-folder access. Adding a device and sharing a folder are distinct permissions. Validate invitations and role changes through the membership workflow.

Resolve and stop#

Inspect conflicts in the Sync conflict view before deleting alternate copies. Pause/Stop affects the project-managed instance, not a personal Syncthing installation. Removing a share configuration is different from deleting its local folder; read confirmations and preserve required content.

Shared current files are not a backup. Use dedicated snapshots for recovery and avoid sharing generated caches that repeatedly trigger rescans.

See also

pages.title: Swarm sessions and secure VPN files
pages.description: Configure Unreal Swarm over WireGuard and exchange files without exposing a public file share.
pages.html:
Swarm session#

Open Swarm over VPN after configuring the project tunnel. Choose Agent or CoordinatorAndAgent, select the matching Unreal executables and existing SwarmAgent.Options.xml, then set coordinator VPN IPv4, local alias, groups, agent filter and optional cache. Apply Agent configuration closes no process: close Swarm Agent yourself first. CyRevision creates a timestamped backup and edits only known fields already present in the XML.

Dns and firewall#

Apply local DNS alias replaces only a marked block belonging to this project in the Windows hosts file. The firewall assistant creates deterministic TCP 8008-8009 rules limited to the WireGuard subnet. Never forward Swarm ports on the modem/router.

Full diagnosis#

Run full diagnosis checks Windows support, the assigned VPN address, executable paths, Agent XML, DNS resolution, project firewall, and both Coordinator ports. Every warning or failure includes a concrete repair step. CyRevisionUnreal also provides Tools > Swarm over VPN for autonomous configuration, process launch and port tests.

Vpn file endpoint#

VPN files binds only to the project WireGuard IPv4 and refuses source addresses outside the project CIDR. Every command requires the 256-bit project token. Choose a private inbox and an explicit shared root, then grant receive, browse and download separately. Send the token to authorized peers through a different trusted channel.

Transfer safety#

Uploads never overwrite an existing file. Uploads and downloads verify the announced size and SHA-256 before an atomic move. Partial files are removed after failure. Absolute paths, parent traversal, junctions and symbolic links cannot escape the shared root. Rotate token immediately revokes old copies and stops the endpoint until restarted.

See also

pages.title: Smart Sync and authorized peers
pages.description: Run an isolated Syncthing instance and exchange signed Git/LFS data with approved devices.
pages.html:
Isolated syncthing#

Each CyRevision project uses its own configuration, database, API key, loopback address, and port. CyRevision never searches for, reconfigures, pauses, or stops a personal Syncthing instance.

Start and stop#

Selecting a Syncthing executable does not start it. Start launches the dedicated project instance. Pause, Resume, and Stop affect only the exact child process created by CyRevision.

Peer admission#

Create a single-use invitation and send its verification code through a separate channel. Approve the returned join request only after checking the device and role. Revocation removes future Git/LFS authorization.

Smart lfs policy#

Current objects are always prioritized. Historical objects can remain on demand, include a configurable number of recent versions, or replicate everything. Signed inventories advertise availability without forcing a download.

See also

pages.title: Sync conflicts and version recovery
pages.description: Resolve concurrent file edits without confusing them with Git merges.
pages.html:
Identify a Sync conflict#

Open Sync > Sync conflicts when the project's synchronization tools are enabled. Concurrent edits can create conflict copies or pending Sync commit conflicts. These are not Git merge markers and should not be resolved blindly through a Git merge command.

Recover deliberately#

  1. Pause editing of the affected file across devices.
  2. Inspect both versions and their timestamps/participants.
  3. Preserve a copy if uncertain, especially for binary assets.
  4. Choose the intended resolution using the offered operation.
  5. Verify the working file and let peers reconcile before resuming edits.

For text, compare content; for binary assets open each candidate in the owning application. A newer timestamp does not guarantee a better version. Sync + Versions may provide older file versions, but its retention is not Git branch history.

Cleanup#

Conflict backup retention and expired-copy cleanup can remove recovery material. Inspect the scope and confirmation first. Test an independent backup restore before relying on synchronization alone: deletions and mistakes can propagate as well as useful changes.

See also

pages.title: CyTask, Jira and ClickUp workflow
pages.description: Configure task providers and verify linked-task transitions after merge.
pages.html:
Enable the provider#

Open Plugins and locate CyTask, Jira or ClickUp. Enable/configure only the installed integration you need. Provider-supplied panels/modes depend on that plugin's capabilities; installing a provider does not connect every project automatically.

Linked tasks in pull requests#

PR > Actions can detect supported task URLs/IDs from PR context such as title, description or branch. Inspect the detected task, provider and project before changing its state. An ambiguous ID alone may need an explicit provider/project mapping.

After merge#

  1. Review the detected references and choose the intended transition.
  2. Prefer manual confirmation while establishing the workflow.
  3. Enable an automatic policy only for a verified project/provider/status mapping.
  4. Merge under the repository's normal permissions.
  5. Check each task update result separately.

A merged PR and a successful task transition are distinct remote operations. One can succeed while the other fails due to permissions, network, missing task or invalid workflow transition. Refresh/check the task before retrying; do not merge again to trigger a task update.

Do not promise a universal Done status: Jira/ClickUp workflows vary by workspace. CyTask's own data and status model can differ from both.

See also

pages.title: Project chat, channels, and private server
pages.description: Discuss in project channels over a VPN, synchronized folder, or your own CyRevision server.
pages.html:
Channel workspace#

The Team chat tab uses project channels, a compact message timeline, attachments, delivery state, and online-member presence. General, development, and builds are available by default. A private server can create additional persistent channels.

Transports#

VPN connects directly to a CyRevision host over a loopback, LAN, or WireGuard address. Sync folder writes immutable per-message files into a synchronized directory and avoids shared-log conflicts. Private server uses the authenticated CyRevision.Server API and keeps the discussion available when team computers are offline.

Private server#

Install CyRevision.Server on a machine you control, set CYREVISION_SERVER_TOKEN, and publish its ASP.NET Core endpoint behind HTTPS. Enter the server URL and token in the project chat settings. Plain HTTP is refused unless the option is explicitly enabled and the address resolves to loopback, LAN, carrier-grade NAT, or a VPN range.

Files and history#

Attachments are size-limited and verified with SHA-256 when stored and downloaded. Server and Sync messages are immutable files grouped by project. Local and synchronized archives can be encrypted. Conversation retention and the attachment limit remain configurable per project.

Security#

Do not publish the direct VPN chat TCP port on a router. For an Internet-facing server, terminate TLS with a trusted certificate and protect the server token like a password. Chat access does not grant Git, Sync, backup, or VPN permissions automatically.

See also

pages.title: System tray and automatic startup
pages.description: Keep optional background services available after hiding the main window.
pages.html:
System tray#

CyRevision exposes a native system tray icon on Windows, macOS, and supported Linux desktops. Click the icon to show or hide the main window. The tray menu shows the selected project and provides Refresh, startup preferences, and an explicit Quit action.

Close and quit#

Close window to tray keeps CyRevision running when the window close button is used. Use File > Exit or Quit CyRevision from the tray to stop the application and dispose its managed services. Disabling the tray also disables close-to-tray and hidden startup.

Automatic startup#

Launch at system login registers CyRevision for the current user only: the Windows Run key, a Linux XDG autostart desktop entry, or a macOS LaunchAgent. Start hidden in tray adds --background so login does not open the main window. The registration always targets the installed executable currently running. Portable builds therefore must stay at the same path.

Linux note#

Tray icons require desktop support for StatusNotifier/AppIndicator. If a Linux desktop does not display tray icons, disable hidden startup so the main window remains reachable.

See also

pages.title: Troubleshooting and safety
pages.description: Diagnose missing tools, failed exchanges, partial transfers, and common repository problems.
pages.html:
Tools not detected#

Confirm that git --version and git lfs version work in a terminal. Restart CyRevision after changing PATH. Syncthing and WireGuard remain optional until their modules are enabled.

Push rejected#

Fetch first and inspect the incoming branch. Never use a force push unless replacing remote history is deliberate and understood.

Pair exchange not moving#

Check that the dedicated Sync instance is running, the peer is connected, and its membership certificate still has a Git-writing role. A file appearing in the exchange folder is not imported unless an authorized signed inventory announces it.

Partial lfs files#

Files ending in .cyrevision-partial are resumable local staging files. Do not rename them into the LFS object store manually. The next exchange verifies the existing prefix and completes or safely restarts the copy.

Safe recovery#

Keep the working tree, active .git directory, backup store, and cold archive as separate locations. Before deleting any data, create a snapshot and verify a restore into a different folder.

See also

pages.title: Local Unreal builds and diagnostics
pages.description: Select target/toolchains, run a bounded build and inspect its output.
pages.html:
Prepare#

Enable Unreal integration and select a detected Unreal project. Open Unreal builds. This workspace runs local engine builds; it is distinct from GitHub Actions and remote build agents.

Configure#

  1. Select the engine version, target, platform and configuration.
  2. Set required SDK/NDK, Java or Linux toolchain paths for that platform.
  3. Choose output directory, timeout and maximum parallel builds.
  4. Enable Cook and package only when that is intended.
  5. Review a preset before applying or saving it.

Auto-configuration helps discover tools; it does not install every proprietary SDK or guarantee license acceptance. Verify the engine/platform requirements in the engine installation.

Execute and inspect#

Use the offered build action or select a version range for batch validation. Results, Errors and warnings, and Full log are separate tabs. Read the full output around a diagnostic; filtered compiler lines can omit the root cause. A successful build for one engine version does not validate all versions in a range.

Builds can consume substantial CPU, RAM and disk. Keep concurrency conservative and do not delete output/toolchain folders while jobs are active. If a target fails before compilation, check project association, installed components and command output before changing source.

See also

pages.title: Optional CyRevision plugin and autonomous Unreal plugin
pages.description: Install CyRevisionUnreal from the app, manage revisions inside Unreal, and connect both sides when desired.
pages.html:
Two separate plugins#

Unreal Engine Integration is an optional CyRevision plugin and is disabled by default. CyRevisionUnreal is an autonomous Editor plugin included in every desktop package.

Compatibility#

The source plugin supports Unreal 4.27 and 5.0 through 5.8 for C++ projects. The Windows package also bundles exact Win64 binaries for Blueprint-only projects on Unreal 5.2 through 5.8. CyRevision detects the engine and project type, displays both compatibility lists, and blocks an unsafe or unavailable installation.

Install from cyrevision#

Open Plugins, enable Unreal Engine Integration, select a .uproject file, then choose Install / update in project. Existing plugin files are moved to Saved/CyRevision/PluginBackups before an update. C++ projects compile the source plugin with their Editor target; Blueprint-only projects receive an exact precompiled variant and do not need C++ project conversion.

Autonomous revision tools#

Tools > Revision dashboard works without CyRevision. It shows Git status and recent commits and can stage, commit, fetch, pull, and push.

Direct connection#

CyRevision creates a random project token under Saved/CyRevision/bridge.json and listens on loopback only. Unreal can notify the matching CyRevision project after Git or advisory changes. Disabling the CyRevision plugin stops the bridge but does not remove the Editor plugin.

Advisory reservations#

Content Browser markers remain informational only: no checkout, permission change, or Git LFS lock is created.

See also

pages.title: WireGuard, services, and Unreal Swarm
pages.description: Create an optional VPN that remains independent from Git and Sync permissions.
pages.html:
Independent module#

VPN can run alone or alongside Git and Sync. Joining a VPN never grants repository or synchronized-folder access automatically.

Backend choice#

System installation uses WireGuard already installed on the machine. Integrated runtime uses official platform components bundled under VpnRuntime and validates every required file against runtime.json SHA-256 hashes. The choice belongs to the project and can only change while its CyRevision tunnel is stopped.

Guided computer setup#

Client-only peers need no inbound firewall or router change. An incoming host opens only its configured WireGuard UDP port. Optional Swarm TCP 8008-8009 and CyRevision control TCP 47831 rules are restricted to the VPN subnet. Diagnose detects the LAN address, gateway and firewall. Windows Defender, UFW and firewalld plans can be applied after explicit administrator confirmation; macOS follows the official application-firewall screen. CyRevision rules use deterministic per-project names and can be removed without touching unrelated rules.

Router / modem#

Reserve the detected LAN address, then forward one external WireGuard UDP port to the same local port. Never forward Swarm or control ports. Test from another network. A private or 100.64.0.0/10 WAN address may indicate CGNAT and require a public server or a public IP from the provider. CyRevision never enables UPnP automatically.

Sync-assisted onboarding#

The current signed invitation or response can be placed in the dedicated Sync exchange. Only signed public VPN payloads are accepted; SHA-256 and signed metadata are checked, secret-shaped fields are rejected, and private keys remain local. Loading a message never joins or accepts it automatically.

Unreal swarm#

Use stable VPN addresses for the Swarm coordinator and agents. Windows Swarm commonly uses TCP 8008 and 8009; the assistant keeps these ports inside the VPN.

See also

pages.title: Mises à jour des releases stables
pages.description: Consulter, télécharger, vérifier et installer une release CyRevision depuis un popup intégré.
pages.html:
Releases uniquement#

Le gestionnaire consulte uniquement la dernière GitHub Release stable de CyRevision. Les commits, branches, brouillons et préversions ne sont jamais proposés comme mises à jour. Les dépôts des projets restent indépendants et ne nécessitent pas GitHub.

Popup de mise à jour#

CyRevision vérifie après le démarrage et affiche un popup lorsqu'une version stable plus récente existe. Le popup présente les notes de version et propose Plus tard, Voir la release et Télécharger et installer. Le bouton Vérifier les mises à jour reste disponible à tout moment.

Paquet de la plateforme#

CyRevision sélectionne l'installateur natif : Setup Windows, paquet DEB Linux x64 ou ARM64, ou image DMG macOS x64 ou ARM64. La page de la release reste accessible si aucun paquet compatible n'est présent.

Installation sûre#

Le paquet est enregistré dans le cache CyRevision et son SHA-256 doit correspondre au manifeste SHA256SUMS.txt. CyRevision programme ensuite un lanceur externe, arrête ses services en arrière-plan et se ferme complètement. Le lanceur attend la fin du processus avant d'ouvrir l'installateur. Aucun git pull du code source n'est effectué.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Différences d'images et d'assets binaires
pages.description: Choisir une comparaison texte, image ou métadonnées selon le fichier.
pages.html:
Choisir une comparaison#

Ouvrez Code & Assets > Asset preview & diff ou un fichier modifié dans Changes/History. Choisissez référence et candidat si proposé. Unified et Side by side comparent du texte ; Images / Heatmap compare les images rendues supportées.

Interpréter#

Ajouts/suppressions montrent des lignes, pas toute leur sémantique. JSON/INI restent du texte même généré. Utilisez le défilement horizontal ; un aperçu borné indique qu'il est incomplet.

Pour les images, comparez versions, dimensions et carte de différences. Zoom/déplacement/ajustement aident à examiner les détails. La heatmap mesure des pixels, pas la pertinence artistique. Gardez les dimensions originales en tête.

Unreal et LFS#

L'aperçu hors ligne .uasset/.umap présente métadonnées et noms détectés, pas une scène rendue complète. Ouvrez l'éditeur propriétaire pour un rendu fidèle. Un pointeur LFS est un petit texte décrivant un objet, pas son image ou son maillage. Récupérez explicitement les contenus manquants.

Open diff in window ou Enlarge garde la comparaison à côté d'un outil. L'aperçu est en lecture seule ; restauration/export sont distincts. Un aperçu indisponible ne prouve pas qu'un asset est corrompu : vérifiez dans son application source.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Backups, rétention et archive froide
pages.description: Créer des snapshots dédupliqués et copier les anciens contenus vers un stockage moins cher.
pages.html:
Snapshots#

Choisissez un emplacement puis créez un snapshot. Les fichiers sont adressés par SHA-256 : un contenu identique n'est stocké qu'une fois. Les caches Unreal et sorties de compilation sont exclus par défaut.

Rétention#

Configurez une chronologie, un nombre maximal de versions, un âge maximal ou un budget de stockage. La rétention est appliquée au stockage actif après la réussite du snapshot.

Restauration#

Restaurez de préférence dans un dossier vide. CyRevision refuse d'écraser les fichiers existants sauf lorsqu'une opération l'autorise explicitement.

Archive froide#

Sélectionnez un disque secondaire, un dossier NAS ou un stockage objet monté, puis un âge d'archivage. Les manifests admissibles et objets manquants sont copiés tout en conservant les snapshots les plus récents dans le stockage actif. L'archivage ne supprime jamais automatiquement la copie active.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Branches et worktrees
pages.description: Examiner avant de changer, fusionner ou supprimer une branche.
pages.html:
Inspecter ou changer#

Ouvrez Git > Branches et actualisez. Distinguez branches locales et références distantes. Sélectionner une ligne l'inspecte ; changer la branche de travail est une action distincte.

Commencer un travail#

  1. Récupérez les références avec Fetch.
  2. Créez une branche au nom explicite depuis la bonne révision.
  3. Basculez puis vérifiez le nom dans l'en-tête.
  4. Faites des commits ciblés et poussez vers le bon remote.

Préservez les fichiers non commitées avant de changer. L'inspecteur parcourt une branche sans modifier le checkout. Un worktree historique crée un autre dossier de travail et consomme du disque. Fermez les éditeurs qui l'utilisent avant son retrait.

Intégrer et ranger#

Comparez avant fusion ou cherry-pick. Appliquez les commits dépendants dans l'ordre. Résolvez ou abandonnez un conflit avant une autre intégration.

Ne supprimez qu'une branche inutile, jamais celle actuellement utilisée. Une PR fusionnée ne prouve pas que tous les commits locaux non poussés peuvent être perdus. PR > Actions propose une suppression locale confirmée lorsque possible : vérifiez la cible. Suppression locale et distante sont distinctes. Ne forcez pas simplement parce que la suppression normale est refusée.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Exécutions CI et logs complets
pages.description: Rechercher dans les logs, filtrer erreurs/avertissements et gérer les runs.
pages.html:
Ouvrir un run#

Ouvrez Git > CI / Actions, actualisez workflows/exécutions et sélectionnez-en une. Les jobs se chargent séparément. Comparez branche, révision et dates : un ancien succès peut coexister avec la dernière compilation en attente/en cours.

Lire le log complet#

  1. Choisissez run et job puis Full log / Logs.
  2. Attendez le téléchargement/extraction.
  3. Choisissez All, Errors ou Warnings. Recherche et gravité se combinent.
  4. Défilez horizontalement ou ouvrez la fenêtre agrandie pour les lignes longues.

Source et numéros de ligne restent visibles. Le classement est heuristique : un filtre Errors vide ne prouve pas la réussite. Revenez à All pour le contexte et lisez la conclusion. Les logs actifs, expirés ou restreints peuvent être indisponibles ; Error summary n'est pas le log complet.

Lancer, relancer, annuler#

Choisissez workflow et référence Git avant le lancement. Le workflow doit accepter le déclenchement manuel. Rerun failed concerne les runs terminés admissibles. Cancel exige les droits Actions/écriture. Le clic droit sur un job peut annuler tout le run parent, pas uniquement ce job : lisez la confirmation. Le serveur vérifie les droits même si l'action apparaît localement.

PR > CI utilise les mêmes lecteur, recherche et filtres. Actualisez après de nouveaux commits. En attente/en cours n'est pas une réussite.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Explorateur, recherche globale et permissions IA
pages.description: Parcourir l'arborescence, chercher avec Ctrl+Shift+F, suivre l'historique d'une sélection et connecter un agent IA facultatif.
pages.html:
Explorateur de code#

L'onglet Code affiche l'arborescence hiérarchique, les métadonnées, l'aperçu texte et les symboles détectés. Les sorties de build, caches Unreal, .git et caches de dépendances sont exclus automatiquement.

Recherche globale#

Ctrl+Shift+F ouvre la recherche depuis toute l'application. La casse, les mots entiers, les expressions régulières et les motifs comme .cs;.cpp sont disponibles. ripgrep est utilisé s'il existe, sinon le moteur .NET prend le relais.

Historique d'une sélection#

Sélectionnez des lignes puis cliquez History of selection. CyRevision suit cette plage inclusive dans Git. Un dossier affiche l'historique de tout son sous-arbre.

Ia facultative#

Activez AI Workspace dans Plugins. Codex CLI, l'API OpenAI Responses, une API compatible, Ollama et LM Studio sont proposés. La clé API reste en mémoire le temps de l'exécution.

Permissions#

La lecture est obligatoire. Modification, réseau, indexation et commit sont séparés. Codex reste en sandbox lecture seule tant que les modifications ne sont pas autorisées. CyRevision effectue lui-même l'indexation et le commit après succès. Aucun push n'est automatique.

OpenCode et configuration du fournisseur#

Le sélecteur IA propose aussi OpenCode CLI. Choisissez OpenCode, réglez l'exécutable (opencode ou son emplacement installé) et le modèle/fournisseur attendu par votre CLI. Codex CLI est distinct : changer de fournisseur ne doit pas conserver le mauvais exécutable. API et modèles locaux exigent leur configuration compatible.

Vérifier un tour#

Choisissez contexte projet et capacités, envoyez la demande, observez l'état et annulez si nécessaire. Examinez les diffs et testez avant d'appliquer/indexer/commiter. Un worktree isolé est un autre checkout, pas une autorisation de publier. Lisez l'état du fournisseur : tous les CLI externes n'imposent pas nécessairement le même sandbox.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Explorateur, aperçus et édition texte
pages.description: Parcourir les fichiers et comprendre les limites des aperçus.
pages.html:
Explorer#

Ouvrez Code & Assets > Solution Explorer. Cherchez un nom/chemin, choisissez Tree/List et affichez les fichiers masqués si nécessaire. Actualisez au besoin ; l'indexation exclut .git, les dépendances et les sorties générées courantes. Un résultat filtré n'est pas l'inventaire complet du disque.

Prévisualiser#

Sélectionnez une ligne. JSON et INI s'ouvrent comme texte, avec coloration selon les formats supportés. Les gros fichiers ont un aperçu borné signalant la troncature ; l'extrait visible n'est pas le fichier complet. Les binaires affichent métadonnées ou aperçu adapté, pas des octets décodés arbitrairement.

Modifier volontairement#

Utilisez l'éditeur proposé, examinez le brouillon et appliquez/enregistrez explicitement. Changer d'onglet ou de sélection n'est pas un commit. Contrôlez Git > Changes puis lancez formatage/compilation dans l'outil concerné. Ne supposez pas un Undo multi-fichiers ou une version enregistrée si l'éditeur ne le propose pas.

Actions sur fichiers#

Clic droit sur le fichier : historique Git / LFS si Git est actif, ou historique Sync dans un projet compatible. Les historiques d'un dossier et d'un fichier ont des périmètres différents. L'aperçu d'asset n'est pas son historique d'auteurs ; celui-ci s'ouvre séparément. Si l'action demande un fichier, resélectionnez sa ligne, pas un titre de dossier.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Console, journaux et état des opérations
pages.description: Distinguer diagnostics de l'app, commandes Git et sortie de compilation.
pages.html:
Où regarder#

Code & Assets > Console & Logs réunit sorties de commandes du dépôt et événements de l'application. Les logs de compilation CI sont dans CI / Actions ou PR > CI ; ceux des builds Unreal locaux dans Unreal builds. Choisir la bonne source évite de confondre un avertissement de l'app avec une erreur du compilateur.

Examiner#

  1. Notez projet sélectionné et heure du problème.
  2. Filtrez texte/gravité si proposé.
  3. Examinez l'opération associée et son état final.
  4. Copiez uniquement l'extrait utile au support.

La barre d'état affiche l'opération courante. Task details ouvre les opérations actives/récentes ; les rafraîchissements ne doivent pas forcer son ouverture. Une analyse annulée par de nouveaux événements disque n'est pas un échec d'écriture.

Console du dépôt#

Les commandes s'exécutent dans le dépôt sélectionné et peuvent modifier fichiers/historique. Lisez paramètres et commande ; ne collez pas une commande destructive inexpliquée issue d'un log ou message. Annuler n'inverse pas une commande déjà terminée.

Les journaux peuvent contenir chemins, arguments et sortie distante. Masquez les identifiants d'accès et travaux non concernés avant partage. N'effacez l'affichage qu'après avoir conservé les éléments de reproduction nécessaires.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Versions de paquets CyStore
pages.description: Examiner les versions publiées et leurs manifestes.
pages.html:
Ouvrir CyStore#

Activez le fournisseur CyStore et sa vue Alpha pour un projet compatible. Configurez les options endpoint/projet proposées puis actualisez les versions. Les versions du dépôt et les releases de mise à jour de l'app sont deux catalogues distincts.

Examiner une version#

  1. Sélectionnez la version et attendez manifeste/fichiers.
  2. Lisez noms, tailles et métadonnées avant de demander le contenu.
  3. Choisissez la destination d'un téléchargement/export proposé.
  4. Vérifiez la fin de l'opération : sélectionner une ligne n'installe rien.

La liste est un manifeste, pas nécessairement une copie locale. La disponibilité dépend du store configuré et des droits du compte. Aucun résultat peut signifier absence de version, filtre, connexion ou droits insuffisants : lisez l'état avant de réessayer.

Périmètre et limites#

CyStore est en Alpha. Utilisez les opérations réellement exposées par le fournisseur installé ; ce n'est pas un client universel de marketplaces. N'écrasez pas un plugin moteur fonctionnel au seul motif d'un numéro supérieur. Vérifiez compatibilité, conservez l'ancienne version et testez le projet consommateur.

Pour mettre à jour CyRevision lui-même, utilisez Help > Check for updates.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Diagnostics de performance et dépannage
pages.description: Recueillir des éléments reproductibles et limiter le travail superflu.
pages.html:
Examiner plutôt que deviner#

Extensions & Help > Diagnostics présente mesures et échantillons récents. Actualisez explicitement ; Clear samples efface les mesures, pas le dépôt. Console & Logs et Task details donnent le contexte des opérations.

Reproduire#

  1. Notez version, système, thème/densité et échelle d'affichage.
  2. Notez mode du projet, vue, filtre et action exacte.
  3. Attendez l'indicateur ou annulez une opération annulable réellement bloquée.
  4. Recommencez sur un petit projet de démonstration et comparez.

Améliorer la réactivité#

Bornez analyses graphe/historique, ciblez les recherches et évitez les scans répétés des sorties générées. Préférez des exclusions adaptées à la désactivation de toute surveillance. Gardez de l'espace sur les disques de cache/build. Réduisez les builds Unreal simultanés si CPU/RAM/disque saturent.

Signaler#

Donnez résultat attendu/observé, étapes minimales et extraits de log utiles masqués. La capture doit montrer vue et chargement. Ne supprimez ni dépôt, sauvegardes ni profil privé pour corriger l'interface. Si elle paraît bloquée, cherchez une confirmation dans une fenêtre auxiliaire et essayez View > Reset panel layout.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Agent de projet Discord
pages.description: Publier les mises à jour Git groupées dans un salon Discord sans dépendre de GitHub.
pages.html:
Webhook du salon#

Créez un webhook entrant dans le salon Discord qui doit recevoir les notifications, puis collez son URL dans l'onglet Agent Discord. Le webhook appartient à un salon précis : CyRevision n'a pas besoin d'un token de bot global.

Modes d'exécution#

Intégré fonctionne dans l'application desktop. Autonome fonctionne dans un sidecar multi-projet et continue après la fermeture du desktop. Lancer l'agent local démarre le sidecar livré ; un serveur ou pair VPN distant peut exécuter le même programme. L'API de contrôle utilise un jeton Bearer, écoute sur loopback par défaut, impose HTTPS à distance et n'autorise HTTP privé qu'après validation explicite d'un VPN WireGuard de confiance.

Point de départ sûr#

Le premier démarrage mémorise le HEAD actuel sans publier l'ancien historique. Les vérifications suivantes regroupent les nouveaux commits dans un message et peuvent signaler les changements de branche active. Les Pull, échanges entre pairs et commits locaux sont détectés dès qu'ils deviennent visibles dans le dépôt Git local.

Anti-doublon#

CyRevision enregistre un point de contrôle par projet uniquement après l'acceptation du message par Discord. Exécutez la surveillance automatique sur un seul agent par projet : deux agents actifs possèdent des points de contrôle locaux indépendants et peuvent annoncer la même mise à jour.

Secrets et mentions#

Le webhook et le jeton de contrôle autonome restent dans la configuration locale de l'utilisateur, hors du projet et du dépôt. L'API ne renvoie jamais le webhook enregistré. Les messages automatiques désactivent les mentions Discord.

Limites#

L'agent annonce l'historique Git visible localement et fonctionne sans GitHub. Les pull requests, issues et reviews appartiennent à une forge et nécessitent l'intégration Discord de cette forge.

Voir aussi

pages.title: Intégrations Unity, Godot et Lore
pages.description: Utiliser le bon adaptateur sans supposer une compatibilité universelle.
pages.html:
Activer le fournisseur adapté#

Dans Plugins, activez Unity, Godot ou Lore selon le besoin. Sélectionnez la racine contenant les métadonnées du moteur. Son espace apparaît si le plugin est actif et la détection réussie.

Configurer et vérifier#

  1. Lisez projet/version détectés.
  2. Choisissez l'exécutable ou fichier demandé par l'adaptateur.
  3. Appliquez et contrôlez l'état avant lancement/installation.
  4. Ouvrez le moteur propriétaire pour valider le résultat.

Chaque adaptateur expose ses fonctions réelles ; les moteurs n'ont pas forcément des possibilités identiques. N'utilisez pas l'installateur Unreal pour Unity/Godot. Activer côté application et installer côté projet sont deux étapes distinctes.

Mode Lore#

Lore est en Alpha et peut fournir son mode, ses branches/historique ou actions de push. Apply/Switch/Push modifient réellement le projet : lisez les confirmations. Ne supposez pas que l'historique Lore est Git si le projet ne l'utilise pas explicitement aussi.

Détection incorrecte#

Contrôlez racine, fichier de métadonnées, plugin et onglets visibles. Un projet moteur imbriqué peut nécessiter son propre dossier plutôt que le parent. Actualisez après modification externe des métadonnées. Si une version n'est pas compatible, conservez l'intégration existante plutôt que forcer un paquet inadéquat.

Voir aussi
pages.text: Activer le fournisseur adapté # Dans Plugins, activez Unity, Godot ou Lore selon le besoin. Sélectionnez la racine contenant les métadonnées du moteur. Son espace apparaît si le plugin est actif et la détection réussie. Configurer et vérifier # Lisez projet/version détectés. Choisissez l'exécutable ou fichier demandé par l'adaptateur. Appliquez et contrôlez l'état avant lancement/installation. Ouvrez le moteur propriétaire pour valider le résultat. Chaque adaptateur expose ses fonctions réelles ; les moteurs n'ont pas forcément des possibilités identiques. N'utilisez pas l'installateur Unreal pour Unity/Godot. Activer côté application et installer côté projet sont deux étapes distinctes. Mode Lore # Lore est en Alpha et peut fournir son mode, ses branches/historique ou actions de push. Apply/Switch/Push modifient réellement le projet : lisez les confirmations. Ne supposez pas que l'historique Lore est Git si le projet ne l'utilise pas explicitement aussi. Détection incorrecte # Contrôlez racine, fichier de métadonnées, plugin et onglets visibles. Un projet moteur imbriqué peut nécessiter son propre dossier plutôt que le parent. Actualisez après modification externe des métadonnées. Si une version n'est pas compatible, conservez l'intégration existante plutôt que forcer un paquet inadéquat. Voir aussi

pages.title: Verrous et réservations de travail
pages.description: Les verrous serveur sont distincts des avis informatifs.
pages.html:
Verrous LFS#

Git > File locks : actualisez le serveur et lisez chemin, propriétaire, date et appartenance. Une entrée en cache ne prouve pas que le serveur est actuellement joignable.

Coordonner une modification#

  1. Vérifiez le verrou avant d'éditer un binaire partagé.
  2. Verrouillez le chemin exact si le workflow le demande.
  3. Modifiez/testez puis commitez et poussez normalement.
  4. Déverrouillez quand l'équipe peut reprendre sans risque.

Libérer le fichier d'un autre ou tous les verrous exige les droits adaptés. Coordonnez-vous et examinez la confirmation. Un commit ne libère pas automatiquement tous les verrous distants. L'application des règles dépend de l'hébergeur et des outils de l'équipe.

Réservations informatives#

Team & Network > Work in progress et les marqueurs du Content Browser Unreal annoncent un travail sur un chemin. Ils ne changent pas les permissions, ne créent pas de verrou LFS et n'empêchent pas l'écriture. Ce sont des outils de coordination, pas une exclusivité garantie.

Actualisez un propriétaire périmé avant de forcer. Si l'accès est refusé, corrigez les droits serveur/compte au lieu de supprimer des métadonnées locales sans rapport.

Voir aussi
